status_message: The paper plane guide is ready.

continuity_bible.workspace_surface: Blue gridded cutting mat providing high visual contrast beneath the white paper and metal ruler.
continuity_bible.lighting: Even, bright overhead studio lighting casting minimal soft shadows across the mat.
continuity_bible.camera_style: Locked first-person overhead camera perspective centered squarely on the cutting mat.
continuity_bible.subject_palette: Crisp white letter/A4 paper and a brushed silver metal Westcott ruler on a blue gridded mat.
continuity_bible.hands_description: Two bare hands entering from the lower frame to steady, fold, and crease the paper.

steps.title: Make the center crease
steps.instruction_text: Place the sheet with a short edge at the top. Bring the two long edges together, press the fold flat, then open the sheet.
steps.narration_script: Fold the sheet lengthwise in half, crease the spine, then open it flat.
steps.pov_video_prompt: The right hand steadies the right side against the mat while the left hand brings the left long edge rightward to meet the right long edge flush, creases vertically down the fold with left fingers, and unfolds the sheet back flat.

physical_state.start_state: A flat rectangular white sheet of paper rests in portrait orientation centered on the blue gridded cutting mat.
physical_state.hand_kinematics: The right hand steadies the right side against the mat while the left hand brings the left long edge rightward to meet the right long edge flush, creases vertically down the fold with left fingers, and unfolds the sheet back flat.
physical_state.end_state: The white sheet lies flat in portrait orientation on the mat with a crisp vertical center valley crease dividing it in half.
verification_cues: A continuous vertical center crease runs straight from the top edge to the bottom edge of the flat sheet.

source_segments.hand_action: Right hand steadies right side of portrait-oriented sheet; left hand brings left long edge over to meet right long edge, creases vertically with left fingers, then unfolds flat.
source_segments.notes: Creates a vertical center reference crease down the sheet.
source_segments.source_title: The Easy and Classic Paper Airplane – The Basic Dart – Fold 'N Fly

tips: Align the corners carefully before pressing the crease so the centerline stays straight.

steps.title: Fold the top corners to center
steps.instruction_text: Fold both top corners down one at a time (2 folds total) so the top edges meet flush along the center crease. Press both triangular flaps flat.
steps.narration_script: Fold both top corners down until their edges meet evenly along the centerline.
steps.pov_video_prompt: The hands pull the top-right corner down and inward until the top-right edge aligns flush along the center crease and flatten the flap, then repeat the diagonal fold and press with the top-left corner.

physical_state.start_state: The portrait white sheet lies flat on the cutting mat with its vertical center crease visible down the middle.
physical_state.hand_kinematics: The hands pull the top-right corner down and inward until the top-right edge aligns flush along the center crease and flatten the flap, then repeat the diagonal fold and press with the top-left corner.
physical_state.end_state: Both top corners form symmetrical flat triangular flaps whose inner edges meet along the center crease into a 90-degree top point.
verification_cues: Two triangular flaps meet flush along the vertical center crease to form a crisp 90-degree point at the top.

source_segments.hand_action: Pulls top-right corner down so top edge meets center crease and flattens; repeats with top-left corner, smoothing both triangular flaps.
source_segments.notes: Top edges align flush along the vertical center crease forming a 90-degree point.
source_segments.source_title: The Easy and Classic Paper Airplane – The Basic Dart – Fold 'N Fly

tips: Keep the two flaps flush at the center without overlapping them.

steps.title: Narrow the nose
steps.instruction_text: Pin the nose in place. Fold each sloping edge onto the center crease, one side at a time, to make a long, narrow point.
steps.narration_script: Fold both angled side edges inward to meet flush along the center crease.
steps.pov_video_prompt: The left hand holds the nose tip steady against the mat while the right hand folds the angled right outer edge inward to meet the center crease and flattens it, then switches hands to fold and flatten the angled left outer edge to the center crease.

physical_state.start_state: The sheet lies flat on the mat with two symmetrical triangular flaps meeting along the vertical center crease.
physical_state.hand_kinematics: The left hand holds the nose tip steady against the mat while the right hand folds the angled right outer edge inward to meet the center crease and flattens it, then switches hands to fold and flatten the angled left outer edge to the center crease.
physical_state.end_state: Two narrower elongated flaps lie flat with their inner folded edges meeting along the center crease to form an acute dart nose.
verification_cues: The front tapers into a sharp acute dart point with both angled edges aligned flush along the center crease.

source_segments.hand_action: Left hand holds nose tip steady while right hand folds angled right outer edge in to center crease; switches hands to fold angled left outer edge to center crease and presses flat.
source_segments.notes: Narrows the front into an acute dart point with folded edges meeting along the center.
source_segments.source_title: The Easy and Classic Paper Airplane – The Basic Dart – Fold 'N Fly

tips: Hold the nose tip as you start each fold so you do not blunt or overlap the sharp point.

steps.title: Fold the body in half
steps.instruction_text: Bring the two halves together along the center crease, enclosing the narrow flaps. Match the tail corners and press the spine from nose to tail.
steps.narration_script: Fold both halves together inward and press firmly from the nose down the keel.
steps.pov_video_prompt: Both hands lift the left and right outer halves upward along the vertical center crease until their edges meet with the inner flaps enclosed, then pinch the sharp nose tip and press firmly down the spine to rest the folded plane on its side.

physical_state.start_state: The paper rests flat on the mat in a symmetrical dart shape with the inner folded flaps facing upward.
physical_state.hand_kinematics: Both hands lift the left and right outer halves upward along the vertical center crease until their edges meet with the inner flaps enclosed, then pinch the sharp nose tip and press firmly down the spine to rest the folded plane on its side.
physical_state.end_state: The plane is folded cleanly in half along the center spine and rests flat on its side on the mat with all inner flap edges hidden inside.
verification_cues: The outer halves sit flush together along the edges with all previous flaps enclosed inside the folded spine.

source_segments.hand_action: Lifts both sides upward along the center crease, bringing outer halves together with inner flaps enclosed, then pinches and runs fingers from sharp nose tip down the spine.
source_segments.notes: Folds plane in half inward, hiding previous flap edges inside.
source_segments.source_title: The Easy and Classic Paper Airplane – The Basic Dart – Fold 'N Fly

tips: Make sure the outer edges line up cleanly as you pinch the spine.

steps.title: Fold the first wing with a ruler
steps.instruction_text: Lay a ruler from the nose toward the middle of the tail. Hold it as a straightedge while you fold the upper layer down, bringing its long outer edge to the bottom of the body.
steps.narration_script: Fold the top wing down over the angled ruler until the crease lies flat.
steps.pov_video_prompt: Hold the ruler from the nose toward the middle of the tail. Fold the upper layer across its edge, slide the ruler out, and press the paper flat.

physical_state.start_state: The folded plane rests flat on its side on the cutting mat with its closed keel along the bottom and sharp nose tip intact.
physical_state.hand_kinematics: Hold the ruler from the nose toward the middle of the tail. Fold the upper layer across its edge, slide the ruler out, and press the paper flat.
physical_state.end_state: One wing lies flat along its new nose-to-tail crease, leaving a strip of folded paper underneath for the keel.
verification_cues: The wing crease starts at the nose. At the tail, the outer wing edge lines up with the lower body edge.

source_segments.technique: First wing fold with ruler guide
source_segments.hand_action: Left hand presses metal ruler angled from nose peak to near bottom rear; right hand folds top wing flap down over ruler edge, slides ruler out, and flattens crease.
source_segments.notes: The ruler runs from the nose toward the middle of the tail edge. The rear keel height is visible, with no marked measurement shown.
source_segments.source_title: The Easy and Classic Paper Airplane – The Basic Dart – Fold 'N Fly
source_segments.analyst_reported_notes: Crease starts at the nose tip and angles slightly above the bottom keel toward the tail (~1.5 cm fuselage height at rear).

tips: Keep the tip of the nose at one end of the straightedge while you position the tail.

steps.title: Match the second wing
steps.instruction_text: Turn the folded plane over. Fold the remaining wing down so its crease and outer edges match the first wing.
steps.narration_script: Flip the plane and fold the second wing down flush with the first wing.
steps.pov_video_prompt: The hands move the ruler aside, flip the plane over onto its folded wing, fold the remaining wing flap downward until its outer edge aligns flush with the first wing, and press firmly along the new fold.

physical_state.start_state: The folded plane rests on its side on the mat with one wing folded down and the metal ruler beside it.
physical_state.hand_kinematics: The hands move the ruler aside, flip the plane over onto its folded wing, fold the remaining wing flap downward until its outer edge aligns flush with the first wing, and press firmly along the new fold.
physical_state.end_state: Both wings are folded down symmetrically with their outer edges aligned flush atop one another on the mat.
verification_cues: The outer edges of both folded wings align directly flush together with matching fuselage height.

source_segments.hand_action: Moves ruler aside, flips plane over, folds remaining wing flap down to align flush with first wing's outer edge, and presses along the fold.
source_segments.notes: Matches wing symmetry directly against the first folded wing without using the ruler.
source_segments.source_title: The Easy and Classic Paper Airplane – The Basic Dart – Fold 'N Fly

tips: Match the wing edges evenly so the plane flies straight.

steps.title: Open the wings
steps.instruction_text: Pinch the center keel from underneath and spread both wings outward horizontally to roughly 90 degrees from the fuselage.
steps.narration_script: Pinch the bottom keel and open both wings out until they sit level.
steps.pov_video_prompt: The hands pinch the center keel from underneath and spread both folded wings outward horizontally until they sit at roughly 90 degrees from the vertical fuselage, setting the plane onto the mat.

physical_state.start_state: The symmetrically folded plane rests on its side on the blue cutting mat with both wings pressed downward.
physical_state.hand_kinematics: The hands pinch the center keel from underneath and spread both folded wings outward horizontally until they sit at roughly 90 degrees from the vertical fuselage, setting the plane onto the mat.
physical_state.end_state: The finished classic dart paper plane rests upright on its center keel on the mat with both wings extending outward horizontally.
verification_cues: Both wings open symmetrically to roughly 90 degrees from the pinched vertical center keel.

source_segments.hand_action: Pinches center keel from underneath and spreads both wings outward horizontally, resting finished plane on mat.
source_segments.notes: Wings open to roughly 90 degrees from the vertical center keel.
source_segments.source_title: The Easy and Classic Paper Airplane – The Basic Dart – Fold 'N Fly

tips: Set both wings at the same horizontal angle for balanced lift.

visual_production.detail: The opening diagram previews the finished dart. A brief generated shot shows the flat sheet and hand placement. The animated center fold follows the publisher’s demonstration. Both unedited generated takes were withheld.

opening.observation: In sample 1, a flat rectangular white sheet of paper rests centered in portrait orientation on a blue gridded cutting mat.

contact.observation: In sample 3, the right hand steadies the right side while the left hand folds the left long edge only halfway to the center of the sheet rather than bringing it flush to meet the right long edge.

result.observation: In sample 7, the left side of the sheet remains folded inward with its raw edge resting down the vertical centerline instead of being unfolded flat to show a single center valley crease.

opening.observation: In sample 1, a flat rectangular white sheet lies centered in portrait orientation on the blue gridded cutting mat.

contact.observation: In sample 5, the right hand covers the right interior of the sheet, blocking the left long edge from meeting the right long edge; the folded left flap stops well short of the right edge while the left fingers press along an off-center curve.

result.observation: In sample 7, the unfolded portrait sheet lies flat on the mat with a smooth surface and no visible vertical center crease from top to bottom edge.

opening.observation: In sample 1, a portrait-oriented white sheet of paper lies flat on a blue gridded cutting mat with a vertical center crease visible down the middle.

contact.observation: In sample 3, the left hand holds the bottom-left area of the sheet steady while the right index finger presses down on the folded top-right triangular flap, aligning its inner edge flush along the vertical center crease; sample 5 subsequently shows both hands pressing down the top-left and top-right triangular flaps symmetrically.

result.observation: In sample 7, both top corners are folded inward into symmetrical triangular flaps whose inner vertical edges meet along the center crease to form a 90-degree point at the top, though the lower edges of the flaps lift slightly casting a shadow on the sheet below.

3.video_model: Animated fold diagram with a Gemini Omni opening shot

visual_production.detail: The opening shows the completed corner folds. The diagram then brings both sloping edges to the center. Both full generated takes folded part of the tail inward.

opening.observation: In sample 1, the white sheet lies flat on the blue gridded mat with two symmetrical triangular top flaps meeting along the vertical center crease above an unfolded rectangular lower section.

contact.observation: In sample 5, neither hand holds the top nose point steady; instead, the right hand rests on the middle-right section while the left hand folds the lower-left vertical edge inward toward the center crease, tapering the bottom edge.

result.observation: In sample 7, the lower rectangular section has been folded into a sharp downward-pointing tip while the top nose remains a broad kite angle rather than narrowing the top angled outer edges into an acute upward dart nose.

opening.observation: In sample 1, the white sheet lies flat on the gridded mat with two symmetrical top triangular flaps meeting along the vertical center crease.

contact.observation: Neither hand holds the top nose tip steady; after folding the bottom-right corner instead of the angled top-right edge in samples 2-3, the left hand folds the left outer edge inward in sample 5 while the right hand rests on the unchanged wide right side.

result.observation: In sample 7, the workpiece is asymmetrical: only the left side forms a narrowed acute edge, while the top-right outer edge remains at its original wide angle rather than folded flush to the center crease.

visual_production.detail: The diagram folds the narrow flaps inside the body, matching the smooth outside face in the source. The unedited generated takes ended with the body open.

opening.observation: In sample 1, the white paper rests flat on the blue gridded mat in a symmetrical dart shape with the inner folded flaps facing upward along the vertical center crease.

contact.observation: In sample 3, both hands fold the left and right outer edges inward toward the center crease to create an additional set of flat dart folds rather than lifting the two halves together to fold the plane in half along the spine.

result.observation: In sample 7, the paper is rotated sideways on the mat as an open symmetrical dart rather than folded in half on its side, leaving both halves spread flat and the inner flap seams exposed along the center crease.

opening.observation: In sample 1, the white paper rests flat on the cutting mat in a symmetrical dart shape with the nose pointing up and the inner folded flaps facing upward.

contact.observation: In sample 5, the left hand holds near the nose tip while the right fingers press along the open center valley crease, leaving both halves spread open with inner flaps exposed instead of folding the outer halves together.

result.observation: In sample 7, the plane lies open on the mat rotated nose-left with both wing halves spread apart and the inner folded flaps fully visible upward, rather than folded in half on its side with flaps enclosed.

visual_production.detail: The straightedge follows the first wing hinge from the nose toward the middle of the tail. The original generated takes had both wings open before the ruler arrived.

opening.observation: In sample 1, the paper plane does not lie flat on its side with a closed keel along the bottom; instead, it rests open and symmetrical on the cutting mat with two splayed wings extending above and below a central horizontal fuselage channel.

contact.observation: In sample 4, the left hand holds the metal ruler across the open lower wing and the right hand presses a fold along the lower section below the central fuselage channel, while the upper wing remains extended upward rather than folded down over a ruler positioned 1.5 cm above a bottom keel.

result.observation: In sample 7, the workpiece remains an open, symmetrical two-winged plane with upper and lower wings splayed out from the central fuselage channel, rather than lying on its side with the top wing flap folded downward above roughly 1.5 cm of exposed bottom fuselage keel.

opening.observation: In sample 1, the paper plane lies opened symmetrically on the cutting mat with upper and lower wing halves spread above and below a central horizontal crease, rather than folded in half on its side with a closed keel along the bottom.

contact.observation: In sample 4, the left and right hands hold a metal ruler diagonally across the lower half of the open plane while the upper wing flap remains untouched and is never folded downward over the ruler edge.

result.observation: In sample 7, the plane remains in the same symmetrical open state as in sample 1 with the upper wing half still extended upward and no downward wing fold or exposed rear fuselage keel created.

visual_production.detail: The diagram turns the folded body over and creases the other wing against the first. The two generated takes started with wings already spread.

opening.observation: In sample 1, the paper plane is resting open with both wings spread outward symmetrically rather than lying on its side with one wing folded down alongside the metal ruler.

contact.observation: In sample 3, instead of folding a remaining wing flap down to align flush with a folded wing on the side, the hands open the fuselage flat and unfold the blunt nose flaps upward into a pointed nose.

result.observation: In sample 7, the plane lies spread open symmetrically across the center fuselage fold with a pointed nose rather than resting on its side with both wings folded flush atop one another.

visual_production.detail: The diagram opens the two wings around the center keel and finishes on a shaded model. The generated take had no automated verdict and finished with the keel projecting above the wings.
